title: Component-dimension rigidity at a Hilbert--Samuel near point of a blowup
statement: Let $X$ be a reduced scheme of finite type over $\mathbf Q$, locally closed in a smooth scheme [def-pc-reduced-scheme, def-weil-finite-type-morphism, def-weil-closed-immersion, def-sbc-smooth-morphisms]. For $z\in X$ put $h_{X,z}(n)=\operatorname{length}(\mathcal O_{X,z}/\mathfrak m_z^{n+1})$ [def-weil-pbc-module-length] and $H_{X,z}=\Lambda^{\operatorname{trdeg}_{\mathbf Q}\kappa(z)}h_{X,z}$, where $\Lambda f(n)=\sum_{i=0}^n f(i)$ [def-kun-transcendence-degree, def-weil-residue-field]. Let $C\hookrightarrow X$ be a smooth closed center on which $H_X$ is locally constant, let $\pi:X'\to X$ be its blowup, with $X'$ the scheme-theoretic strict transform in an ambient blowup [def-nagata-global-blowup, def-nagata-strict-transform], and let $y\in X'$ map to $x\in C$. Write $P_X(x)=\{\dim Z:Z\text{ an irreducible component of }X,\ x\in Z\}$, using topological Krull dimension [def-weil-irreducible-components, def-kun-topological-krull-dimension], and define $P_{X'}(y)$ similarly. If $H_{X',y}=H_{X,x}$ as sequences, then $P_{X'}(y)=P_X(x)$. Components contained in $C$ and hence absent from the strict transform are allowed in the hypotheses; equality of the Hilbert--Samuel functions is essential.

source.place: VIII 2.3.13, printed p.94, synchronization discussion. WANTED: BMT arXiv:0905.3580 section 6.3 and its near-point/normal-flatness input for the equality case of permissible Hilbert--Samuel blowup comparison. No Stacks tag states this equality-case theorem.

proof.text: Apply lem-trf-strict-transform-component-closures to q=i composed with p and I. It identifies every upstairs component with T(W)=closure(pi inverse-image of (W minus C)) for an original component W meeting the complement, and gives dim T(W)=dim W. No Hilbert--Samuel hypothesis is needed here.

For every original component W through x=pi(y), apply lem-trf-hilbert-samuel-near-component-incidence using the given local constancy and equality of functions. This gives y in T(W). It also implies W minus C is nonempty: otherwise its inverse image and its closure would both be empty.

Prove the equality of dimension sets by extensionality. An upstairs component through y is T(W) by step 1. Since W is closed and pi is continuous, T(W) is contained in pi inverse-image of W; therefore x=pi(y) belongs to W. Step 1 identifies their dimensions. Conversely, for W through x, step 2 puts y in T(W) and proves W minus C nonempty. Step 1 now makes T(W) an upstairs component of the same dimension. These two constructions prove both inclusions.
